# DAWG Code of Conduct

## Our commitment

DAWG is a public project maintained by Slaviors Group. We want issue reports,
discussions, and every other project interaction to be respectful, useful, and
safe for everyone.

This repository is publicly available for transparency, learning, and local
use. Maintainers are not accepting external code, documentation, translation,
design, or dependency contributions. That policy does not prevent anyone from
reporting a reproducible defect through the supported issue form.

## Expected behavior

When participating in DAWG spaces, please:

- communicate constructively and in good faith;
- focus reports and discussion on observable technical behavior;
- respect differing experience levels, identities, and viewpoints;
- protect privacy by removing credentials, personal data, private URLs, and
  sensitive artifact contents before posting; and
- follow the repository's issue and contribution policies.

## Unacceptable behavior

The following is not acceptable:

- harassment, threats, discriminatory language, or personal attacks;
- spam, advertising, trolling, or deliberately disruptive behavior;
- publishing private, identifying, credential, or confidential information
  without permission;
- submitting malicious content, exploit payloads, or unsafe attachments without
  prior coordination; or
- using issues, pull requests, or discussions to bypass the maintainer-only
  contribution policy.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to GitHub Issues, Discussions, pull requests,
project comments, and other spaces where someone represents or participates in
DAWG.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit, hide, lock, or remove content; close issues or pull
requests; and block participation when behavior violates this Code of Conduct.
For conduct concerns, use GitHub's **Report content** control rather than
posting the report publicly. Reports will be handled as privately as the
available GitHub tools permit.
